overview: Muscogee histories connect ancestral places such as Ocmulgee with a changing confederacy of towns and the continuing Muscogee Nation in Oklahoma.

items.text: Town business took place in council houses beside ceremonial plazas. A meko governed with advisers.
Maternal clans shaped membership, while people also maintained loyalties to particular towns.
Chunkey yards and ball-play grounds stood near town ceremonial centers.
Eighteenth-century commerce changed as the deerskin trade replaced the earlier slave trade, reshaping relations with colonial traders.
Following forced removal in the late 1830s, a national government formed in 1840. A constitution followed in 1867, with Okmulgee as capital.
Ocmulgee remains an ancestral homeland of the Muscogee Nation, whose government continues in Oklahoma.
